course.description.source: Investigate how people in Southeast Asia lived, connected across seas, faced changing power, built new nations, and preserve their histories. Explore real objects, archives, places, photographs, and different points of view.
course.description.note: Five "อย่างไร" clauses in a row mirror the English list; a reviewer may prefer a shorter, smoother sentence. "Investigate" is ศึกษา, "Explore" is สำรวจ.
course.description.back: Study how people in Southeast Asia lived, how they were connected across the sea, how they faced changing power, how they built new nations and how they keep their histories. Explore real objects, archives, places, photographs and different points of view.

sections.0.title.back: Evidence and connections in the early era

sections.0.question.source: What do objects and places tell us about early lives and trade by sea?
sections.0.question.back: What do objects and places tell us about the lives of people in the early era and about sea trade?

sections.0.description.source: Study a pot from Ban Chiang, old boat planks from Butuan and maps of Melaka, and learn to tell what a source shows from what we guess.
sections.0.description.note: Butuan is บูตวน (Thai Wikipedia form). "learn to tell what a source shows from what we guess" is ฝึกแยกสิ่งที่แหล่งข้อมูลแสดงให้เห็นออกจากสิ่งที่เราเดา.
sections.0.description.back: Study a pot from Ban Chiang, the planks of an old boat from Butuan and a map of Melaka, then practise separating what a source shows from what we guess.

sections.1.question.source: Who gained, who worked, and who challenged unfair rules?
sections.1.question.note: "challenged unfair rules" is ท้าทายกฎที่ไม่ยุติธรรม; ต่อต้าน (resisted) would be stronger than the English.
sections.1.question.back: Who benefited, who did the work, and who challenged unfair rules?

sections.1.description.source: Follow nutmeg from Banda, rubber from Malaya and letters from Kartini, and ask whose story each source tells.
sections.1.description.note: Kartini is การ์ตีนี (some Thai sources write การ์ตินี); Malaya is มาลายา (some write มลายา); nutmeg is จันทน์เทศ; Banda is บันดา. The lesson translators must use the same spellings.
sections.1.description.back: Follow nutmeg from Banda, rubber from Malaya and Kartini's letters, then ask whose story each source tells.

sections.2.question.source: How did war and independence change different communities?
sections.2.question.back: How did war and independence change the lives of different communities?

sections.2.description.source: See how war changed daily life in Singapore, compare how Indonesia and Malaya became independent, and look at how Timor-Leste rebuilt its schools.
sections.2.description.note: Malaya is มาลายา (check against SAT08). Timor-Leste is ติมอร์-เลสเต as in KEY_TERMS.
sections.2.description.back: See how war changed everyday life in Singapore, compare how Indonesia and Malaya got independence, and see how Timor-Leste built schools again.

sections.3.question.source: How do people choose which stories to keep and share?
sections.3.question.back: How do people choose which stories to keep and share?

sections.3.description.source: Visit the port of Hội An and the temple of Borobudur, then plan a small exhibition that tells a shared history fairly.
sections.3.description.note: Hội An is ฮอยอัน. "port" uses the key term ท่าเรือ. "temple of Borobudur" is ศาสนสถานบุโรพุทโธ: วัด suggests a Thai monastery with monks, and มหาสถูป/เจดีย์ are possible alternatives; a reviewer should choose.
sections.3.description.back: Visit the port of Hoi An and the religious site Borobudur, then plan a small exhibition that tells a shared history fairly.
